- `GET /invite/{token}` (Application.php:1079-1081) redirects → `/app/invite/{token}` which has NO Vue route → SPA no-match/404. `InviteLinkController::showAcceptInvitePage` (renders accept-invite.tpl) is DEAD (no longer routed).
- Redeem: `POST /api/v1/me/invite-links/{token}/redeem` (InviteLinkController::redeem) is AUTH-GATED (401 auth.required if no user; 201 LibraryShare on success; 400 invalid_invite; 404 invite_link_not_found; 410 invite_expired_or_exhausted). No public redeem endpoint exists and none is needed.
- accept-invite.tpl behavior: unauth → login/signup CTAs (redirect back to /invite/{token}); auth → single "Accept Invite" button → POST redeem → on success redirect /app/shared-with-me; JS maps 401/410/404. NO invite metadata displayed (generic "You've been invited to access a library!").

Hub redirect (Application.php:1080) becomes CORRECT once page exists — no server change.
- BLOCKER for auth flow: `LoginForm.vue:54-55` always `router.push(config.home)` and IGNORES `route.query.redirect` (guard sets redirect at createPhlixApp.ts:77 but nothing consumes it). `/home/sites/phlix/phlix-ui/src/utils/safeRedirect.ts` is a sound open-redirect guard, and the design is defense-in-depth on two independent layers:

1. The value must be a non-empty `string` (arrays/undefined from `route.query.redirect` return `null`), must NOT start with `//` or `/\`, and MUST start with `/app/`. That rejects absolute URLs (`https://evil`), protocol-relative (`//evil`), and backslash tricks (`/\evil`).

Vue Router resolves a string location as an in-app path against the current origin; it cannot cross origins even for adversarial input like `/app/%2f%2fevil` or `/app/../..`. So any `/app/`-prefixed weirdness that slips past layer 1 is still just an internal (likely 404) route, not an external redirect.

Encoded escapes (`%2f%2f…`) don't bypass: the check runs on the decoded `route.query.redirect` string, and even if they did, router navigation stays same-origin. The `/app/` prefix check is sufficient given the SPA-navigation constraint.

 * so the admin section gets its own navigation chrome without the host shell
 * having to render a nested menu. Every page — and the layout itself — is a
 * lazily-imported chunk, so a consumer that never shows admin doesn't pay for it.
 *
 * **Page groups (H0).** Admin pages are exported as three registries so each app

 * - {@link serverAdminPages} — media-server-only: Dashboard, Webhooks, Services,
 *   Integrations, Backup, Cast Devices, DLNA, Remote Access, Live TV, Collections,
 *   History, SyncPlay, Libraries, Duplicates, Plugins.
 * - {@link hubAdminPages} — hub-only: Hub Dashboard, Audit Logs.

 * `buildAdminRoutes(base)` with no `pages` argument yields the **server pages in
 * their original sidebar order** (Dashboard first), so the server's admin landing
 * page and sidebar ordering are unchanged (U6 adds Plugins after Libraries).
 * `buildServerAdminRoutes` is the explicit synonym for that default;
 * `buildHubAdminRoutes` mounts the hub set (Hub Dashboard, Users, Logs, Settings,
 * Audit Logs). Each child keeps a stable `admin-*` route name and resolves to

<script setup lang="ts">
/**
 * AcceptInvitePage (WS-D-HUB #7) — the PUBLIC invite-acceptance surface.
 *
 * Reached at `/app/invite/:token`, where the hub redirects the public
 * `GET /invite/{token}` link. This is the only genuinely broken hub surface: the
 * PHP redirect had no matching Vue route (404). This restores parity with the
 * retired Smarty `home/accept-invite.tpl` + `accept-invite.js` flow:
 *
 *   - NOT logged in → generic "you've been invited" message + Log In / Sign Up
 *     buttons that carry a `?redirect=/app/invite/<token>` hop back here (honoured
 *     by LoginForm/SignupForm's safe-redirect guard) so the user returns to accept.
 *   - Logged in → an "Accept Invite" button → `POST /api/v1/me/invite-links/{token}/redeem`
 *     (auth-gated). On success a confirmation + a "View Shared Libraries" button
 *     to `/app/shared-with-me`. Errors map: 401 re-login, 404 not found, 410
 *     expired/exhausted, else generic.
 *
 * The route is `meta: { public: true }` so the auth guard lets an unauthenticated
 * visitor reach it. `isLoggedIn` here is only a token-PRESENCE flag (the public
 * route skips `auth.init()`); a stale token simply surfaces as a 401 on redeem,
 * which routes the user to log in again — matching the Smarty behaviour.
 *
 * `client` is an injectable test seam; it defaults to the shared `api` singleton.
 */
import { ref, computed } from 'vue';

{"stdout":"## Unreleased

### Changes
- chore(cleanup): remove the dead `src/api/music.ts` module (zero importers; `fetchArtists`/`fetchAlbumsByArtist`/`fetchTracksByAlbum` were superseded by the `ApiClient` music methods). Never bundled, so no `dist/` rebuild — internal source cleanup only.


## v0.82.0 (2026-07-18)

### Changes
- feat(admin/logs): overhaul the log renderer — emit separate **channel** and **level** badges (the full Monolog/PSR-3 level set mapped onto five colour tones), no more duplicated level text
- feat(admin/logs): show timestamps in the viewer's **local time** as `h:mm:ss.<micros>AM/PM` (12-hour), splicing sub-second precision back from the raw ISO (JS `Date` truncates to ms) and dropping the date when the entry is from today
- feat(admin/logs): strip the `-YYYY-MM-DD.log` rotation suffix from filenames (accepts both the Monolog hyphen separator and the legacy dot separator)
- feat(admin/logs): **cross-file line combine** now fires — the parser populates source/timestamp/message so identical lines across multiple files merge into a single row with a comma-joined source list
- fix(admin/logs): defensively strip a redundant legacy inline `[LEVEL] datetime ` prefix from message bodies
- fix(admin/logs): fix message **double-escape** (`highlightJson` already escapes `& < >`, so the message is no longer escaped twice) and HTML-escape the channel/source fragments before `v-html` (the XSS boundary for raw log content)
- test(player): refresh stale QualityMenu/quality/shortcuts specs left behind by earlier feature commits (closest-level-≥-source contract, the q/Q quality shortcut, and the variant-id emit); only a stale docstring changes in product code


## v0.81.0 (2026-07-18)

### Changes
- feat(detail): "Play Trailer" button with in-app YouTube embed modal (validated key/URL)
- feat(detail): title-logo hero overlay (falls back to text title; handles local PNG or remote SVG)
- feat(admin/profiles): content-rating cap picker

- **Hub-to-hub federation** — federate with peer hubs to share libraries across hubs, with
  per-peer sessions and admin delegation.
- **Media requests** — a Jellyseerr-class request queue. Users request movies/series; admins
  approve, and the Hub talks to Sonarr/Radarr to fulfil them.
- **Web UI & admin console** — the hub's front door is a Vue SPA (the shared `@phlix/ui` design
  system) served at `/app` (`/` redirects to `/app/servers`): My Servers, Federation, and Shares for
  every signed-in user, plus a `requiresAdmin` **admin console** at `/app/admin/*` (Hub Dashboard,
  Users, Logs, Settings, Audit Logs). The original Smarty pages are deprecated and will be removed
  in a future release. Everything is backed by a full JSON API under `/api/v1` (incl. `/api/v1/admin/*`).
- **Operations-ready** — structured JSON logging (Monolog) across dedicated channels
  (app, error, hub, relay, audit), a `/health` endpoint, and idempotent SQL migrations.

## Architecture

The Hub runs as a set of long-lived [Workerman](https://www.workerman.net/) workers in a single
process group:

| Worker | Default port | Purpose |
|--------|--------------|---------|
| HTTP | `8800` | REST API + the Vue SPA (`/app`) + legacy SSR pages + `/health` |
| Relay (server-facing) | `8802` | Servers connect here to open their outbound tunnel |
| Relay (client-facing) | `8803` | Remote clients connect (`GET /client/{server_id}`) and are routed down a tunnel |

Supporting pieces:

- **PSR-11 container** (PHP-DI 7) wires services; routes are registered in
  [`src/Application.php`](src/Application.php).
- **MySQL** is accessed through an async connection pool (`workerman/mysql`). The pool is
  initialised lazily so `/health` stays up even if the database is briefly unreachable.","numLines":30,"s

{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/sites/phlix/phlix-server/README.md","content":"`php bin/phlix migrate` is the supported equivalent of `php scripts/run-migrations.php` — both delegate to the same `Phlix\Common\Database\MigrationRunner` service, applying every `migrations/*.sql` file on each run (idempotent; no tracking table). More commands are added in later steps.

### Admin SPA (admin-ui)

The admin console is a **React + TypeScript + Vite** single-page app. Its source lives in
`admin-ui/`; the production build is emitted into `public/assets/admin/` and **committed to the
repo**, so the running Workerman server has **no Node build dependency at runtime** (it just serves
the static shell + bundle). `admin-ui/node_modules/` is gitignored.

The SPA mounts at `/admin` and `/admin/*`, served by `AdminAppController` (returns the built
`index.html` shell; 503 if the bundle is missing) and gated by the existing `AdminMiddleware` — a
non-admin (401/403) is redirected (302) to `/login`. Its typed `ApiClient` reuses the same JWT
mechanism as `public/assets/js/api-client.js` (`access_token`/`refresh_token` in `localStorage`,
Bearer header, single retry on 401 via `POST /auth/refresh`).

```bash
cd admin-ui
npm install          # one-time / on dependency changes
npm run build        # tsc + vite build → ../public/assets/admin/ (commit the result)
npm run test         # Vitest unit/component tests
npm run dev          # Vite dev server (HMR) for local development
```

When you change anything under `admin-ui/src/`, re-run `npm run build` and commit the refreshed
`public/assets/admin/` bundle along with your source changes.

CI runs the SPA build + Vitest suite on any change under `admin-ui/` via the **Admin UI** GitHub
Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/admin-ui.yml`): `npm ci → npm run build → npm run test` on
push/PR to `master`/`main`/`develop` (path-filtered, so PHP-only changes don't trigger it).

{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/sites/phlix/phlix-docs/docs/clients/web.md","content":"# Web Portal

**Since:** 0.18.0

> [!TIP]
> The Phlix web portal runs in any modern browser — no software to install. Navigate to your server's web address, sign in with your Hub account or enter a direct server URL, and start streaming immediately. Works on Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge.

## Install / Store Links

- **No installation required** — open the URL in your browser and start using it
- **Supported browsers:** Chrome 110+, Firefox 115+, Safari 16+, Edge 110+
- **Mobile browsers:** Fully functional but optimized for desktop

Bookmark your server's web portal URL:
```
https://your-server-domain.com/web
```
Or for local access:
```
http://192.168.1.100:32400/web
```

## Platform-Specific Notes

- The web portal requires the server's web address to be reachable from your browser — either on the local network or via a Hub relay / reverse proxy.
- Some browser extensions (ad blockers, privacy extensions) may interfere with playback. If playback does not start, try disabling extensions or using an incognito/private window.
- For best playback performance, use a browser with hardware acceleration enabled (Chrome and Edge have this on by default).

**Since:** 0.19.0

## TL;DR

Invite links let you share access to a library (or all libraries) on one of your claimed servers with anyone — no hub account required on their end. You set the permission level, a maximum number of uses, and an expiry. The recipient visits the link, logs in or creates a hub account, and immediately sees the shared library under **"Shared with me"**.

---

## The Invite Links Page

Invite links are managed through the Hub API (the `/api/v1/me/invite-links`
endpoints below) and the legacy `/invite-links` page. They are not in the current
SPA top navigation (My Servers / Federation / Shares) — the public acceptance link
`/invite/{token}` that you send to recipients is unchanged.

The invite-links view lists every invite link you have created, one card per link:

```
┌─ Invite Link ──────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Server: My Server                     [Copy URL] [✕]│
│ Library: All Libraries · Permission: Read · Uses: 0/1 │
│ Expires: Jun 5 2026 · Created: May 29 2026           │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Reading a link card

Each card shows:

- **Server** — the claimed server this link targets.
- **Copy URL** — copies the invite URL to your clipboard. The button briefly shows "Copied!" after a successful copy.
- **Revoke (✕)** — deletes the invite link immediately. The card disappears from the list and the URL no longer works.
- **Library** — either "All Libraries" or the specific library name. A link for all libraries is created when `library_id` is not set.
- **Permission** — `Read` or `Read/Write`. Shown as a coloured badge.
- **Uses** — `X / Y` where `Y` is the maximum uses you set and `X` is how many times the link has been used. A link with `X = Y` shows an **Exhausted** badge and the revoke button remains available.
- **Expiry*

## [Unreleased]

### Web UI
- **WS-D — owner/user surfaces migrated to the `/app` Vue SPA (Smarty retirement pending owner verification).**
  The hub's owner/user surfaces — **My Servers**, **Server Detail**, **Federation**, **Federation Shares**,
  **Shares**, **Shared With Me**, **Invite Links**, and **Requests** (plus the admin request-approval queue) —
  are now served by the shared `@phlix/ui` Vue SPA at `/app/*`, alongside the existing admin console at
  `/app/admin/*`. Route + nav registration lives in `web-ui/src/main.ts`. The equivalent Smarty SSR pages
  remain in place and are **not** removed — deletion is deferred until the new `/app` pages are verified live.
- **WS-D — public invite acceptance route `/app/invite/:token` (fixes the previously-broken `/invite/{token}` 404).**
  The public `GET /invite/{token}` link now redirects to the SPA `AcceptInvitePage` (`meta.public`, so an
  unauthenticated invitee reaches it without the auth guard). Not logged in → Log In / Sign Up buttons that
  carry a safe `?redirect=/app/invite/<token>` hop back here; logged in → an **Accept Invite** button calling
  `POST /api/v1/me/invite-links/{token}/redeem`, then a **View Shared Libraries** link to `/app/shared-with-me`.
  This restores parity with the retired Smarty `accept-invite` flow, whose PHP redirect had no matching Vue route.
- **WS-D — safe post-auth redirect.** `LoginForm`/`SignupForm` now honour a validated internal `?redirect`
  query (via the shared `@phlix/ui` `safeRedirect` guard, which only accepts same-origin `/app/` paths), so
  logging in / signing up from the invite page returns the user to accept the invite. Vitest specs cover all
  of the above pages.

### Added

- **WS-D — media SPA pages are now reachable under `/app` (Smarty retirement pending owner verification).**

  **Search** (`/app/search`), and the **Music** sub-pages (`/app/music/artists`, `/app/music/artist/:name`,
  `/app/music/album/:name`, `/app/music/tracks`, `/app/music/player`), plus nav links (Music, Books,
  Audiobooks, Photos, Search). The passkey/WebAuthn surface is now a **Security** tab on the SPA Settings
  page (`/app/settings/security`) rather than a standalone page. The equivalent Smarty SSR templates and
  their routes remain in place — deletion is deferred until the migrated `/app` pages are verified live.
- **SV-3.3 — loudness normalization + client capability negotiation.**

# Docs authoring

## New pages must be registered in the sidebar

A new `.md` file under `docs/` does not appear in site navigation on its own —
add a matching entry to the sidebar array in `docs/.vitepress/config.ts`:

```ts
{ text: 'SSO (OIDC & LDAP)', link: '/security/sso-oidc-ldap' },
{ text: 'JWKS API', link: '/reference/api/hub-jwks' },
```

Links are site-root-relative and omit the `.md` extension.

## The build is the link gate

`docs/.vitepress/config.ts` sets `ignoreDeadLinks: false`, so a bad internal link
or heading anchor (including cross-page `page#heading-slug`) fails the build
instead of warning. Run after any edit that adds or changes links or headings:

```bash
npm run docs:build
npm run docs:preview
```

## API reference pages

Pages under `docs/reference/api/` pair a prose `.md` with a machine-readable
OpenAPI `.yaml` sibling — e.g. `docs/reference/api/hub-jwks.md` alongside
`docs/reference/api/hub-jwks.yaml` — and the prose page references the spec by
path.

# Library Metadata & Ratings

**Phase:** P1-S9

Phlix implements a comprehensive rating and metadata system that supports numerical ratings, smart collection rules, fuzzy title matching, and multi-language metadata fallback.

## Numerical Ratings

### Rating Scale

Ratings use a **0-10 scale** internally, displayed in the UI as stars or numeric values depending on context.

| Internal Value | Star Display | Numeric Display |
|---------------|--------------|-----------------|
| 0 | No stars | 0.0 |
| 1-2 | ★☆☆☆☆ | 1-2 |
| 3-4 | ★★☆☆☆ | 3-4 |
| 5-6 | ★★★☆☆ | 5-6 |
| 7-8 | ★★★★☆ | 7-8 |
| 9-10 | ★★★★★ | 9-10 |

### Rating Storage

Ratings are stored in the `media_items` table:

- `rating` — Community rating (float 0.0-10.0)
- `user_rating` — Per-user personal rating (int 1-10, nullable)

## Sorting & Filtering

### Sort by Rating

```http
GET /api/v1/media?sort=rating&order=desc&limit=50
GET /api/v1/media?sort=rating&order=asc&limit=50
```

**Parameters:**
- `sort=rating` — Sort by community rating
- `order=asc|desc` — Sort direction (default: desc)

### Filter by Minimum Rating

```http
GET /api/v1/media?min_rating=7.5
```

This returns only items with a community rating >= 7.5.

## Smart Collection Rules

Smart collections use flexible rule-based filtering:

### Rule Types

| Rule | Field | Example |
|------|-------|---------|
| Genre | `genres[]` | `genres[]=Action&genres[]=Sci-Fi` |
| Decade | `yearFrom`, `yearTo` | `yearFrom=1980&yearTo=1989` |
| Rating Threshold | `min_rating` | `min_rating=8.0` |
| Year Range | `yearFrom`, `yearTo` | `yearFrom=2010` |

### Example: High-Rated 80s Action Movi

# Reference

Complete reference material for Phlix. If you are looking for task-oriented
guides instead, start at [First Run](/first-run) or the
[Developer docs](/developers).

## API

- [Server API Reference](/reference/api) — the full REST API: endpoints,
  WebSocket events, authentication, and plugin hooks.
- [WebAuthn / Passkey API](/reference/api/auth-webauthn) — registration and
  authentication ceremonies for passkey login.
- [JWKS API](/reference/api/hub-jwks) — the Hub's JSON Web Key Set endpoint,
  used to verify Hub-issued tokens.
- [Media Requests API](/reference/api/hub-media-requests) — the Hub media
  request flow (Radarr / Sonarr integration).

## Configuration

- [Environment variables](/reference/env-vars) — every supported variable and
  its default.
- [Config files](/reference/config-files) — file locations, formats, and
  precedence.
- [Admin Reference](/reference/admin-reference) — administrative settings and
  what each one changes.

## Command line & protocols

- [CLI Reference](/reference/cli) — every command, flag, and exit code.
- [Skip Button Protocol](/reference/skip-button-protocol) — the wire format
  clients use for intro/outro skip.

## See also

- [Server architecture](/dev/architecture-server) — how the pieces fit together.
- [Event reference](/dev/event-reference) — events emitted across the system.
- [Plugin SDK](/dev/plugin-sdk) — plugin internals.

# The Hub

The Hub connects your Phlix server to the outside world: remote access without
port forwarding, and library sharing with people you trust.

New here? Start with [What Is the Hub?](/hub/what-is-the-hub).

## Getting connected

- [What Is the Hub?](/hub/what-is-the-hub) — what it does and why you might want it.
- [Claim your server](/hub/claim-server) — link a server to your Hub account.
- [Server Detail](/hub/server-detail) — the per-server view and what it reports.
- [Remote Access Without Relay Tunnel](/hub/remote-access) — direct connections
  when you do not need the relay.

## Sharing

- [Share Libraries with Friends and Family](/hub/share-with-friends)
- [Library Sharing](/hub/library-sharing) — per-library permissions.
- [Invite Links](/hub/invite-links)
- [Media Requests](/hub/requests) — Radarr / Sonarr integration.

## Running your own Hub

- [Self-Host the Hub](/hub/self-host-the-hub)
- [Hub Admin guide](/hub-admin/overview) — operating a Hub for others.

git push -u origin feat/section-landing-pages 2>&1 | tail -2 && env -u GITHUB_TOKEN -u GH_TOKEN gh pr create --title "Add section landing pages so bare /reference, /hub etc. resolve" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Why

Five sections have a directory but no sibling page, so **`/reference`, `/developers`, `/hub`, `/hub-admin` and `/dev` all 301 to a trailing slash and then 404** — VitePress emits no directory index.

The `phlix-website` brand-kit sites link to exactly those bare paths **537 times**, 430 of them to `/reference` alone (anchor text: "API reference" ×383). Those are the single largest class of broken links in that repo.

## Why this fixes it without touching the 50 sites

GitHub Pages already resolves extensionless URLs, and **a sibling `<name>.html` takes precedence over `<name>/`**. That's verifiable on the live site today:

| URL | Status |
|---|---|
| `/phlix-docs/libraries` | **200** (because `docs/libraries.md` exists) |
| `/phlix-docs/libraries/` | 404 |
| `/phlix-docs/libraries.html` | 200 |

So adding these five pages repairs **528 of the 537** links with zero changes to the sites themselves.

## These are real pages, not redirect stubs

`/reference` in particular was genuinely unreachable: **the nav bar has no Reference entry**, so all nine pages under `reference/` — including the full "Phlix Media Server API Reference" — could not be found from the homepage at all. That's also why an earlier audit concluded no API reference existed; it does, at `/reference/api.html`.

Each landing page groups its section's real pages under headings and cross-links neighbouring sections:

- **`/reference`** — API (server API, WebAuthn, JWKS, media requests), configuration (env vars, config files, admin reference), CLI and the skip-button protocol.
- **`/developers`** — live TV/tuners/DVR, streaming & playback, media analysis, metadata/collections/playlists, plugins & theming.
- **`/hub`** — getting connected, sharing, running your own Hub, plus relay internals for contributors.
- **`/hub-admin`** — install & first boot, networking & TLS, operations, policy & compliance.
- **`/dev`** — architecture, protocols & schemas, client builds, workflow.

A **Reference** nav entry is added so that section is discoverable.

## Sidebar note

The landing pages live at `/<section>` with no trailing slash, so they do **not** match the existing `'/<section>/'` sidebar keys and need their own entries. Longest-prefix matching keeps `'/hub-admin/'` winning over `'/hub'` for pages inside `hub-admin/`.

## Verification

`npm run docs:build` clean. That's a real gate here — `ignoreDeadLinks: false` fails the build on any bad internal link or heading anchor, so every cross-link in these five pages is confirmed to resolve. All five routes emitted (`dist/reference.html` etc.) and no directory route clobbered (`reference/api.html`, `hub-admin/overview.html`, `hub/what-is-the-hub.html`, `dev/architecture-server.html`, `developers/dvr.html` all still built).

Remaining 9 of the 537 are one-off typos in the sites (`user`, `guide`, `developer`, `plugins`, `installation`, `api`, `development`) and are better fixed there.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -2

7:## 3. Post-upgrade library rescan
8:
9:After a major version upgrade, metadata provider behaviour may change (e.g. TVDb → TMDb priority shifts). A full rescan re-reads **every** file from disk instead of skipping unchanged ones:
10:
11:```bash
12:# List the libraries to get their ids
13:sudo -u phlix php bin/phlix library:list
14:
15:# Full rescan — one library at a time (there is no "all libraries" flag)
16:sudo -u phlix php bin/phlix library:scan {libraryId} --rescan
17:
18:# Watch the scan progress
19:tail -f .logs/media.log
20:```
21:
22:The equivalent from the admin UI is **Admin → Libraries → Rescan**, or
23:`POST /api/v1/libraries/{id}/rescan`; those queue the job for the background
24:worker instead of blocking your shell.
25:
26:::: tip A rescan does not delete anything
27:It re-reads every file, then prunes **only** items whose source file is gone.
28:Items, watch history and fetched metadata are preserved. On a large **music**
29:library, expect it to take substantially longer than a plain scan — see
30:[Scan vs Rescan](../admin/library-management#scan-vs-rescan-vs-match-metadata)
31:for measured figures.
32::::
33:
34:### When is a full rescan required?
35:
36:| Upgrade type | Rescan needed? |
37:|-------------|----------------|
38:| Patch (e.g. 0.18.0 → 0.18.1) | No — migrations handle schema changes |
39:| Minor (e.g. 0.17.x → 0.18.x) | Recommended — metadata provider updates may change match behaviour |
40:| Major (e.g. 0.x → 1.x) | Yes — review breaking changes first |
41:
42:If items that were previously matched are now unmatched after a rescan, the item's metadata shape changed in the upstream provider. Delete and re-add the item to force a fresh metadata fetch.
43:

## Reviewer (per-step) — 2026-07-27

### 1. BLOCKING — "a rescan re-reads EVERY file" is true only for MUSIC libraries

`docs/admin/library-management.md:179`
> "**Rescan** | Re-reads **every** file from disk — no skipping — then prunes only the
> items whose source file has disappeared … to repair bad/duplicated matches — anything
> where the existing rows are wrong."

For every non-music library type the scanner **skips an already-indexed path outright**.
`MediaScanner::processScanBatch()` (`src/Media/Library/MediaScanner.php:772-775` at
`b8a0bd7e`):

```php
if (isset($existingByPath[$path])) {

    $this->backfillItemSourceMetadata($existingByPath[$path]);

and the same early return in `MediaScanner::processFile()` at `MediaScanner.php:1306-1318`
(`return false; // Already scanned`). Nothing re-parses the filename, re-derives the
title/year, or re-fetches metadata for that row — only a *missing*-source-metadata
backfill runs.

`LibraryManager::rescanLibrary()` (`src/Media/Library/LibraryManager.php:911-951`) is
`scanLibrary($libraryId, $onProgress, readEveryFile: true)` + `pruneRemovedItems()`, and
`readEveryFile` is consumed by the music path only —
`LibraryManager.php:535-537`: *"`$readEveryFile` is deliberately unused from here down:
every other scanner has no skip index, so there is nothing for the flag to switch off."*
The diff's own `docs/dev/library-scan-worker.md` states this correctly ("Every other
scanner ignores the flag"), which is exactly what the user-facing pages contradict.

matches" and "when hunting a file the incremental scan is silently passing over". On a
movie/TV library that is false — the rescan skips the same row, and the repair never
happens. `docs/faq.md:20` sends a user with an unmatched item down this path (its own
step 3 then contradicts it by telling them to delete and re-add the item, which *is* the
working remedy).

{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/sites/phlix/phlix-docs/docs/admin/library-management.md","content":"## Fixing a single item's match

When a single movie, series, season, or episode is matched to the wrong metadata —
or never matched at all — an admin can correct it without re-scanning the whole
library. A **Match metadata** action appears (for admins only) on media cards across
Browse and library pages, and on the detail/series page hero.

Clicking it opens a modal that:

- **Auto-searches** TMDB on open using the item's current title and year (TV vs movie
  is derived from the item type — series/season/episode search TV, everything else
  searches movies).
- Lets you **refine the query** with a manual title and optional year and re-search.
- Shows the candidate results (poster, title, year, type badge, overview) with a
  **Use this** button per result.

Picking a result resolves and persists the chosen metadata for that item (and, for a
**series**, walks its seasons and episodes to enrich the whole subtree), then refreshes
the card/page in place with the new poster and details.

If TMDB has no API key configured, the modal shows a clear "configure a TMDB API key"
message instead of empty results.

This is backed by two admin-gated endpoints:

```http
GET  /api/v1/media/{id}/match/search?query=&year=&type=
POST /api/v1/media/{id}/match/apply
```

- `GET .../match/search` returns up to 20 candidates as
  `{ results: [ { tmdb_id, type, title, year, overview, poster_url, backdrop_url, vote_average } ], query, type, context }`.
  All query params are optional — the server derives `query`/`year`/`type` from the
  item when omitted.
  The `context` block provides source-file context for the current item:
  `{ original_filename?, path?, parsed_title?, year?, tags? }` — only non-null/non-empty
  keys are included. `original_filename` is the original raw filename or `basename(path)`;
  `path` is the file path (max 500 chars); `

| Priority | Source | Notes |
|----------|--------|-------|
| 1 (highest) | Local NFO | `movie.nfo` in the same folder |

| `S01E01` or `1x01` | TV episode | `Show Name S01E01.mkv` |
| `Season 00/` or `Specials/` folder | TV (specials) | `Season 00/` |

take hours. On a **movie, TV, photo, book or audiobook** library an
already-indexed path is not re-parsed or re-matched at all; the scan does a
missing-source-metadata backfill on that row and moves on. To repair a match on

|---|---|

library for one rescan**. Once the prune has removed the row, the *next* scan or

docs(S149): correct rescan semantics across the site — 3 review rounds

The docs described `rescan` as "destructive — purges every item, then rescans
from scratch". It is a full re-read followed by a prune of only those items whose
source file is gone; rows are upserted in place and keep their UUID.

Correcting that surfaced a chain of further false claims, each found by a review
round or by re-grepping rather than by working the previous round's list.

Corrected:
- "rescan re-reads every file" is true of MUSIC libraries only. `$readEveryFile`
  is consumed by the music path and nothing else; every other scanner has no skip
  index, and an already-indexed path only gets a source-metadata backfill.
- `scripts/run-library-scan-worker.php --full-rescan` never existed. It was
  recommended on five pages. The script takes start|stop|restart|status.
- `library:scan --all` does not exist and `libraryId` is required.
- Running two scan consumers is NOT safe: the startup reaper fails every `running`
  row with no library filter and no age guard.
- A rescan does not "mark items unavailable" — the prune DELETEs them, behind a
  per-root presence guard.
- An interrupted rescan does not resume: full-read works by not loading the skip
  index, and an unloaded index reports nothing as unchanged.
- Music provider enrichment: MusicBrainzProvider/AudioDbProvider do not exist.
  Music types are deliberately absent from MetadataManager and a music refresh is
  a graceful no-op; only the optional plugin remains, on MediaItemAdded.
- The video-library "mtime-based checksum" and "folder watcher queues a rescan"
  claims are both false — MediaScanner has no mtime logic, and FolderWatcher's
  change loop has no production caller.
- The metadata cache claim, twice: it is not 24 hours, and it is not absent
  either. MetadataHttpClient caches 2xx bodies for one hour, singleton-scoped, so
  it spans jobs.

Added, because the site documented no working remedy for a bad match:
- match-metadata / refresh-metadata / clear-metadata, with the type filter stated:
  the matcher handles movie, video and series only, so a metadata job on a photo,
  book or audiobook library completes having processed zero items. The `0 / n`
  progress reading is the observable tell.
- Movie and series failure modes are documented separately — the series resolver
  takes no external ids, so clear-metadata does not help it.
- A danger notice for moving a file (S158): a moved top-level row is matched by a
  path-independent canonical key, its `path` is never updated, and the prune in
  the same run deletes it, cascading user_item_data. Stated as a defect with no
  safe workaround rather than a supported flow.

Documented for the first time: the CLI scan job row from S150, and the measured
rescan runtimes (9h55m -> 28m41s on 61,135 tracks), explicitly labelled a single
measurement and not a per-track rate.

EOF

tool_input.command:
env -u GITHUB_TOKEN -u GH_TOKEN gh pr create --base master --head s149-rescan-semantics --title "S149 — correct rescan semantics across the site" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Problem

The docs described a library `rescan` as **"destructive — purges every item, then rescans from scratch"**, and warned that continue-watching positions were lost. That is not what it does: it re-reads every file, then prunes only items whose source file is gone. Rows are upserted in place and keep their UUID, so referencing user data survives.

Correcting that surfaced a chain of further false claims. Each was found by a review round or by re-grepping — **not** by working the previous round's list, which was incomplete every time.

## Corrected

- **"Rescan re-reads every file" is true of MUSIC libraries only.** `$readEveryFile` is consumed by the music path and nothing else; every other scanner has no skip index, and an already-indexed path only gets a source-metadata backfill. Nine pages had generalised it to all types.
- **`run-library-scan-worker.php --full-rescan` never existed** — recommended on five pages. The script takes `start|stop|restart|status`.
- **`library:scan --all` does not exist** and `libraryId` is required. This was on the first-run page.
- **Running two scan consumers is not safe** — the startup reaper fails every `running` row with no library filter and no age guard, so a second consumer stamps the first's live job `failed`.
- **The prune DELETEs items; it does not "mark them unavailable."**
- **An interrupted rescan does not resume.** Full-read works by *not loading* the skip index, and an unloaded index reports nothing as unchanged. This claim was inherited verbatim from a server code comment that is also wrong.
- **Music provider enrichment does not exist.** `MusicBrainzProvider`/`AudioDbProvider` are absent from the tree; music types are deliberately excluded from `MetadataManager` and a music refresh is a graceful no-op.
- **Video "mtime-based checksums" and "the folder watcher queues a rescan" are both false.** `MediaScanner` has no mtime logic at all, and `FolderWatcher`'s change loop has no production caller.
- **The metadata cache claim, twice.** It is not 24 hours — and it is not absent either. `MetadataHttpClient` caches 2xx bodies for **one hour**, singleton-scoped, so the cache spans jobs.

## Added

The site documented **no working remedy** for a bad or missing metadata match — `faq.md` sent users with an unmatched movie to a rescan that skips that exact row.

- `match-metadata` / `refresh-metadata` / `clear-metadata` are now documented, **with the type filter stated**: the matcher handles `movie`, `video` and `series` only, so a metadata job on a photo, book or audiobook library completes having processed **zero** items. The `0 / n` progress reading is the observable tell.
- Movie and series failure modes are documented **separately** — the series resolver takes no external ids, so `clear-metadata` does not help it.
- Nothing re-matches a photo, book or audiobook item. Stated plainly rather than substituting a command that silently does nothing.

## A product defect, documented as one

Moving a top-level file loses its watch history. The scanner matches the moved row by a **path-independent canonical key**, returns without updating its `path`, and the prune in the same run deletes it — cascading `user_item_data` via a real FK. Filed as **S158**; documented as a defect with **no safe workaround**, not as a supported flow. Episodes and music are unaffected.

## Verification

`npm run docs:build` green. `ignoreDeadLinks: false`, so every new and moved anchor is link-checked.

Three review rounds; rounds 1 and 2 both found over-scoping, round 3 found none — the remaining findings were a different class.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -2
